subproblem.title: Coordinate k-planes: dimension k and unit orientations ±e_ι
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let ι : Fin k → Fin P be strictly increasing. Put τ_j := e_{ι(j)} = EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 (standard basis vectors of Euclid P) and V := span{τ_j : j ∈ Fin k}. Then finrank V = k. Moreover, there is a k-vector e ∈ MultiVector P k (a continuous linear functional on k-covectors) with e(α) = α(τ_0, …, τ_{k−1}) for every k-covector α, such that both e and −e are unit orientations of V (IsUnitOrientationOf).

Source: step 4(i) of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im (“τ := E_p is orthonormal (EuclideanSpace.orthonormal_single composed with the injective ι), span(range τ) = V_p, and ξ(x)(α) = sign(β_p)·α(τ) for all α, with sign(β_p) ∈ {1, −1}”). It also covers “finrank V_p = k (finrank_span_eq_card; E_p is linearly independent)” from step 4(iii), and the k-vector e_p := (α ↦ α(E_p)) of the Notation paragraph.

Notation. τ_j := EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 for j ∈ Fin k, and V := span_ℝ(range τ).

1. τ is orthonormal. The standard basis i ↦ EuclideanSpace.single i 1 of Euclid P is orthonormal: it is the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), or equivalently use EuclideanSpace.orthonormal_single. Since ι is strictly increasing, it is injective, so τ = (standard basis) ∘ ι is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp).
2. finrank V = k. An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent). So finrank_ℝ span(range τ) = card(Fin k) = k (finrank_span_eq_card, Fintype.card_fin).
3. The k-vector e.
 - Let ev(α) := α(τ_0, …, τ_{k−1}) for α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) k, the continuous alternating k-linear maps Euclid P → ℝ.
 - ev is linear: addition and scalar multiplication of alternating maps are pointwise, so ev(α + β) = ev(α) + ev(β) and ev(cα) = c·ev(α) hold by definition.
 - ev is bounded: |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ ∏_j ‖τ_j‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), and ‖τ_j‖ = 1 because τ_j is a standard basis vector. So |ev(α)| ≤ 1·‖α‖.
 Hence e := LinearMap.mkContinuous ev 1 is a continuous linear functional, i.e. e ∈ MultiVector P k, and e(α) = α(τ) for every α. This is the first property of e.
4. IsUnitOrientationOf e V. Take τ as the witness. It is orthonormal (step 1), span(range τ) = V by definition, and e(α) = α(τ) for all α. This is the first alternative of the definition.
5. IsUnitOrientationOf (−e) V. Take the same witness τ. Negation of continuous linear maps is pointwise, so (−e)(α) = −e(α) = −α(τ) for all α. This is the second alternative. ∎ For k = 0, τ is the empty family, V = {0}, finrank V = 0, and e evaluates a 0-covector at the empty tuple; every step holds verbatim.

subproblem.title: Open lattice faces are disjoint, and their union is flat near each of its points
subproblem.statement: Assume (FG), the exact frozen Lean type of Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_geometry: for all P, k, the open unit cube has volume 1, and for index pairs p, q with strictly increasing first components the face maps are isometries, have diameter ≤ √P on the closed cube, and an open face point Φ_p(y) is at distance ≥ 1 or ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j) (some j) from any point Φ_q(y') of a different closed face. Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let S be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b), with b ∈ ℤ^P and ι : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing for every p ∈ S. Write Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ Euclid k, Q₁ := (0,1)^k, F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁), C := ⋃_{q∈S} F̆_q and V_p := span{e_{ι(j)} : j ∈ Fin k}. Then (a) F̆_p ∩ F̆_q = ∅ for distinct p, q ∈ S; and (b) for every p ∈ S and t ∈ Q₁ there is δ > 0 such that every z ∈ Euclid P with dist(z, Φ_p(t)) < δ satisfies z ∈ C ⟺ z − Φ_p(t) ∈ V_p.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 4(ii) of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im: the open faces F̆_p are pairwise disjoint, and C ∩ B(x, δ) = Π_p ∩ B(x, δ). The isometry and separation facts come from the antecedent (FG). (FG) is verbatim the frozen type of Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_geometry, the selected node's resolved sibling dependency; the parent discharges (FG) with that declaration.

Notation. For p = (ι, b): Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 b + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ Euclid k, with e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Also Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}, F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁), C := ⋃_{q∈S} F̆_q and V_p := span_ℝ{e_{ι(j)} : j ∈ Fin k}. Every p ∈ S has a strictly increasing first component.

0. Facts from (FG), applied at (P, k). For pairs p, q whose first components are strictly increasing:
 (iso) dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') = dist(y, y') for all y, y' ∈ Euclid k;
 (sep) if p ≠ q, y ∈ Q₁ and y' ∈ [0,1]^k, then 1 ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y'), or min(y_j, 1 − y_j) ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') for some j.
1. Part (a), disjointness. Let p ≠ q in S, and suppose w ∈ F̆_p ∩ F̆_q, say w = Φ_p(t) = Φ_q(t') with t, t' ∈ Q₁. Since Q₁ ⊆ [0,1]^k, (sep) applies to (p, q, t, t'). But dist(Φ_p t, Φ_q t') = dist(w, w) = 0. The first alternative gives 1 ≤ 0, which is false. The second gives min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ 0 for some j, which is false because 0 < t_j < 1. So F̆_p ∩ F̆_q = ∅.
2. Part (b), choice of δ. Fix p = (ι, b) ∈ S and t ∈ Q₁, and let x := Φ_p(t). Let D be the finite set {1} ∪ {min(t_j, 1 − t_j) : j ∈ Fin k}; it is nonempty because it contains 1. Put δ := min D. Every element of D is positive, so δ > 0. Also δ ≤ 1, and δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for each j. (For k = 0, D = {1} and δ = 1.)
 Now let z ∈ Euclid P with dist(z, x) < δ. We show z ∈ C ⟺ z − x ∈ V_p.
3. (⇒) Suppose z ∈ C, so z = Φ_q(t') for some q ∈ S and t' ∈ Q₁.
 - If q ≠ p, apply (sep) to (p, q, t, t'); this is allowed since t' ∈ Q₁ ⊆ [0,1]^k. It gives 1 ≤ dist(x, z), or min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ dist(x, z) for some j. But dist(x, z) = dist(z, x) < δ, with δ ≤ 1 and δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j). So both alternatives are impossible.
 - Hence q = p. Then z − x = Φ_p(t') − Φ_p(t) = Σ_j (t'_j − t_j) e_{ι(j)}, because the constant toLp(b) cancels. This is a linear combination of the e_{ι(j)}, so z − x ∈ V_p (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun, with coefficients t'_j − t_j).
4. (⇐) Suppose z − x ∈ V_p.
 - V_p is spanned by the finite family (e_{ι(j)})_{j ∈ Fin k}, so there is c : Fin k → ℝ with Σ_j c_j e_{ι(j)} = z − x (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun).
 - Let t' := t + toLp(c) ∈ Euclid k, so t'_j = t_j + c_j. Then Φ_p(t') = toLp(b) + Σ_j t_j e_{ι(j)} + Σ_j c_j e_{ι(j)} = x + (z − x) = z.
 - By (iso), dist(t', t) = dist(Φ_p t', Φ_p t) = dist(z, x) < δ. A coordinate distance is at most the Euclidean distance (PiLp.dist_apply_le), so |c_j| = |t'_j − t_j| ≤ dist(t', t) < δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for each j.
 - Hence t'_j = t_j + c_j > t_j − min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≥ 0, and t'_j < t_j + min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ 1. So t' ∈ Q₁ and z = Φ_p(t') ∈ F̆_p. Since p ∈ S, z ∈ C.
5. Steps 3 and 4 prove the equivalence for every z with dist(z, x) < δ. This completes part (b). ∎

subproblem.title: A finite disjoint family of oriented rectifiable pieces gives an IMRep with additive action and mass
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, I a type, U ⊆ Euclid P, and S ⊆ I finite. For each p ∈ S let F_p ⊆ Euclid P be Borel with F_p ⊆ U and Hᵏ(F_p) < ∞, let m_p ∈ ℕ be positive, ξ_p ∈ MultiVector P k a k-vector, and G_p : Euclid k → Euclid P a Lipschitz map with F_p ⊆ range G_p. Suppose the F_p (p ∈ S) are pairwise disjoint, and at every x ∈ F_p some subspace Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_p Q, where C := ⋃_{q∈S} F_q. Then there is an IMRep R in U of dimension k such that R.action(ω) = Σ_{p∈S} m_p ∫_{F_p} ξ_p(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U), and R.measure(Euclid P) = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p). Here Hᵏ = μHE[k].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (I : Type) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : Finset I) (F : I → Set (Euclid P)) (m : I → ℕ) (ξ : I → MultiVector P k) (G : I → Euclid k → Euclid P), (∀ p ∈ S, MeasurableSet (F p)) → (∀ p ∈ S, F p ⊆ U) → (∀ p ∈ S, μHE[k] (F p) ≠ ∞) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, p ≠ q → Disjoint (F p) (F q)) → (∀ p ∈ S, 0 < m p) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K (G p)) → (∀ p ∈ S, F p ⊆ range (G p)) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∀ x ∈ F p, ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (⋃ q ∈ S, F q) x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ p) Q) → ∃ R : IMRep U k, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) = ∑ p ∈ S, (m p : ℝ) * ∫ x in F p, ξ p ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μHE[k]) ∧ R.measure univ = ∑ p ∈ S, (m p : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[k] (F p)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–6 of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im: the triple (C, θ, ξ), its IMRep fields, the splitting of the action integral over the disjoint pieces, and the computation of R.measure. Here they are stated for an arbitrary finite family of disjoint pieces. The parent instantiates it with the open faces F̆_p = Φ_p((0,1)^k), m_p = |β_p|, ξ_p = sign(β_p) e_p and G_p = Φ_p. The contract's IMRep encodes Simon, Ch. 6, Definition 3.1, and IMRep.action encodes 6.3.1 (‡).

Notation. Hᵏ := μHE[k] on Euclid P, and C := ⋃_{q∈S} F_q.

1. Carrier. C is Borel, as a finite union of Borel sets (Finset.measurableSet_biUnion). C ⊆ U because each F_q ⊆ U.
2. Uniqueness of the piece. If p, q ∈ S, q ≠ p and x ∈ F_p, then x ∉ F_q, by the disjointness hypothesis.
3. Multiplicity. Let θ(x) := Σ_{q∈S} 1_{F_q}(x) · m_q ∈ ℕ, the sum of the indicators of the F_q with constant values m_q.
 - θ is measurable: each summand is the indicator of a Borel set with a constant value, and a finite sum of measurable ℕ-valued functions is measurable (Finset.measurable_sum).
 - θ(x) = m_p for x ∈ F_p with p ∈ S: by step 2 every other summand vanishes (Finset.sum_eq_single).
 - Hence θ > 0 on C, since every point of C lies in some F_p with m_p > 0.
4. Orientation. List S as p₁, …, p_N (S.toList). Define ξ(x) := ξ_{p_i} for the least i with x ∈ F_{p_i}, and ξ(x) := 0 if x ∉ C. Formally, ξ(x) is the right fold over the list of (q, acc) ↦ (if x ∈ F_q then ξ_q else acc), starting from 0.
 - By induction on the list, ξ is strongly measurable: the empty fold is constant, and each step is an if-then-else on a Borel set between a constant and a strongly measurable function (StronglyMeasurable.ite). So ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞C.
 - ξ(x) = ξ_p whenever x ∈ F_p and p ∈ S, by step 2 and induction on the list: every entry q ≠ p has x ∉ F_q, and the entry p returns ξ_p.
 By disjointness this ξ is the same function as the supplied proof's Σ_{q∈S} 1_{F_q} ξ_q; the fold only changes how it is written. In Lean the sum route through Finset.stronglyMeasurable_sum needs ContinuousAdd (MultiVector P k), and that instance does not synthesize in the frozen environment (checked).
5. Countable rectifiability.
 - With the list p₁, …, p_N, define F_j := G_{p_{j+1}} for j < N, and F_j := the constant map 0 for j ≥ N. Each F_j is Lipschitz, by hypothesis or because it is constant.
 - Every x ∈ C lies in some F_p ⊆ range G_p, and p = p_{j+1} for some j < N. So C ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with M₀ := ∅, and Hᵏ(∅) = 0.
 This is CountablyRectifiable k C. (Equivalently: countablyRectifiable_range for each G_p, then countablyRectifiable_iUnion and CountablyRectifiable.mono, as in the supplied proof.)
6. Total weight. The F_p (p ∈ S) are pairwise disjoint and Borel, so ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} ∫⁻_{F_p} θ dHᵏ (lintegral_biUnion_finset). On F_p, θ = m_p by step 3, so ∫⁻_{F_p} θ dHᵏ = m_p Hᵏ(F_p) (setLIntegral_congr_fun, lintegral_const, Measure.restrict_apply_univ). Hence ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p), which is finite because every Hᵏ(F_p) < ∞ (ENNReal.sum_ne_top, ENNReal.mul_ne_top).
7. Local integrability. For every compact K ⊆ U, ∫⁻_{C∩K} θ dHᵏ ≤ ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ < ∞ (lintegral_mono_set).
8. Orients. Let x ∈ C, so x ∈ F_p for some p ∈ S. The hypothesis gives Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_p Q, and ξ(x) = ξ_p by step 4. So the orients condition holds at every point of C. Since C is Borel, it holds Hᵏ⌞C-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_forall_mem).
9. Steps 1 and 3–8 verify every field of IMRep U k for R := (C, θ, ξ).
10. Action. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U), and write ω also for the underlying form. It is C^∞, hence continuous, with compact support. By definition, R.action(ω) = ∫_C θ(x) · ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x).
 - For p ∈ S let g_p(x) := m_p · ξ_p(ω(x)). g_p is continuous, since ξ_p is a continuous linear functional. Its support lies in the support of ω, because ξ_p(0) = 0, so g_p has compact support.
 - Hᵏ⌞F_p is a finite measure, hence finite on compact sets, so g_p is integrable for it (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
 - On F_p the integrand θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) equals g_p(x), by steps 3 and 4. Since F_p is Borel, the integrand is integrable on F_p (IntegrableOn.congr_fun).
 - The Bochner integral is additive over finitely many pairwise disjoint Borel sets (integral_biUnion_finset). So R.action(ω) = Σ_{p∈S} ∫_{F_p} θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} ∫_{F_p} m_p ξ_p(ω(x)) dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p ∫_{F_p} ξ_p(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) (setIntegral_congr_fun, integral_const_mul).
11. Mass measure. R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞C).withDensity θ. So R.measure(Euclid P) = ∫⁻ θ d(Hᵏ⌞C) = ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p), by withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_univ and step 6. ∎ If S = ∅, then C = ∅, θ = 0 and ξ = 0: every field holds trivially, and both identities read 0 = 0.

subproblem.title: Isometric images: Borel, Hᵏ-measure and change of variables
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let Φ : Euclid k → Euclid P be an isometry for the Euclidean metrics, and let A ⊆ Euclid k be a Borel set. Then Φ(A) is Borel, Hᵏ(Φ(A)) = Lᵏ(A), and ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHᵏ = ∫_A h(Φ(y)) dy for every function h : Euclid P → ℝ. Here Hᵏ = μHE[k] is Mathlib's normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure, Lᵏ = volume is Lebesgue measure on Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), and the integrals are Bochner integrals (each is 0 when its integrand is not integrable).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (Φ : Euclid k → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid k)), Isometry Φ → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet (Φ '' A) ∧ μHE[k] (Φ '' A) = volume A ∧ ∀ h : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ x in Φ '' A, h x ∂μHE[k] = ∫ y in A, h (Φ y)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of the selected node dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im (“Change of variables. Φ_p is an isometry, hence a closed embedding and a measurable embedding … F̆_p is Borel; ∫_{F̆_p} h dHᵏ = ∫_{Q₁} h(Φ_p y) dy …; Hᵏ(F̆_p) = vol(Q₁) = 1”). It is stated here for an arbitrary isometry Φ and Borel set A; the parent applies it with Φ = Φ_p and A = Q₁. The same type is frozen in the twin branch (root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.…polyhedral_im-a1) under the name cmcdtfrpi_isometry_image_integral. That name is reserved there, so this child is declared under the fresh name Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfrpi_isometry_image_integral and proved here.

Notation. Hᵏ := μHE[k], on Euclid P or on Euclid k as indicated; Lᵏ := volume on Euclid k; μ⌞S := μ.restrict S; Φ_#μ := μ.map Φ.

1. Measurable embedding. Euclid k is complete and Φ is an isometry, so Φ is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding). A closed embedding between Borel spaces is a measurable embedding (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding): Φ is injective and measurable, and it maps Borel sets to Borel sets. Hence Φ(A) is Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image). This is the first conclusion.
2. Hᵏ = Lᵏ on Euclid k, by EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume k.
3. Measure of the image. Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries, for every set: Hᵏ(Φ(A)) = Hᵏ(A) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). By step 2, Hᵏ(A) = Lᵏ(A). This is the second conclusion.
4. Push-forward identity: Hᵏ⌞Φ(A) = Φ_#(Lᵏ⌞A) as measures on Euclid P.
 - For a measurable embedding and every set E, (Φ_#μ)⌞E = Φ_#(μ⌞Φ⁻¹(E)) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map). Apply it with μ := Hᵏ on Euclid k and E := Φ(A).
 - Φ_#Hᵏ = Hᵏ⌞range Φ (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). So the left side is (Hᵏ⌞range Φ)⌞Φ(A) = Hᵏ⌞(Φ(A) ∩ range Φ) (Measure.restrict_restrict; Φ(A) is Borel by step 1), and this is Hᵏ⌞Φ(A) because Φ(A) ⊆ range Φ.
 - On the right side, Φ⁻¹(Φ(A)) = A by injectivity (Set.preimage_image_eq), and Hᵏ⌞A = Lᵏ⌞A by step 2.
5. Change of variables. For a measurable embedding Φ, every measure μ on Euclid k and every function g : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ g d(Φ_#μ) = ∫ g∘Φ dμ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). No measurability or integrability hypothesis is needed: g is AE-strongly measurable for Φ_#μ exactly when g∘Φ is for μ, integrability transfers in the same way, and otherwise both Bochner integrals are 0. Take μ := Lᵏ⌞A and use step 4: ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHᵏ = ∫ h d(Hᵏ⌞Φ(A)) = ∫ h d(Φ_#(Lᵏ⌞A)) = ∫_A h(Φ(y)) dy. This is the third conclusion.
6. No case distinction is needed. For k = 0, Euclid 0 is a single point and the same lemmas apply verbatim. ∎

subproblem.title: A set that coincides with x + V near x has approximate tangent space V at x
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ Euclid P be an arbitrary set, x ∈ Euclid P, V a linear subspace of Euclid P with finrank V = n, and δ > 0. Suppose that every z ∈ Euclid P with dist(z, x) < δ satisfies z ∈ M ⟺ z − x ∈ V. Then V is the approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4, as formalized by SimonGMT's HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V. That is, finrank V = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(Euclid P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_V f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺, where η_{x,r}(y) = blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹(y − x) and Hⁿ = μHE[n].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → 0 < δ → (∀ z : Euclid P, dist z x < δ → (z ∈ M ↔ z - x ∈ V)) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(iii) of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im. There, for 0 < r < δ/R, the blow-ups of the carrier agree with V_p on B(0, R), so r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(C)} f dHᵏ is eventually equal to ∫_{V_p} f dHᵏ along 𝓝[>] 0. Here it is stated for an arbitrary set M and subspace V; the local hypothesis is exactly what step 4(ii) provides for the carrier. It generalizes SimonGMT's hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean), which is the case M = V, x ∈ V.

Notation. η_{x,r}(y) := blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹ • (y − x), and Hⁿ := μHE[n] on Euclid P. By definition, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V means: finrank ℝ V = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(Euclid P, ℝ) the function r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ tends to ∫_V f dHⁿ along 𝓝[>] 0.

1. finrank ℝ V = n is a hypothesis. Fix f ∈ C_c(Euclid P, ℝ) for the rest of the proof.
2. A ball outside which f vanishes. tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B̄(0, R₀) for some R₀ ∈ ℝ. Put R := max(R₀, 0) + 1. Then R > 0 and R > R₀. If ‖y‖ ≥ R, then y ∉ B̄(0, R₀) ⊇ tsupport f, so f(y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence f vanishes outside the open ball B := B(0, R).
3. Localization. For every set S ⊆ Euclid P, measurable or not, ∫_S f dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩S} f dHⁿ. Indeed B is open, hence Borel, so (Hⁿ⌞S)⌞B = Hⁿ⌞(B ∩ S) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Since f = 0 off B, ∫ f d((Hⁿ⌞S)⌞B) = ∫ f d(Hⁿ⌞S) (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
4. Claim: if r > 0 and rR < δ (equivalently 0 < r < δ/R), then B ∩ η_{x,r}(M) = B ∩ V.
 (⊆) Let y ∈ B with y = r⁻¹(z − x) for some z ∈ M. Then ‖y‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖ < R, so ‖z − x‖ < rR < δ, i.e. dist(z, x) < δ. By the hypothesis, z ∈ M gives z − x ∈ V. Since V is a subspace, y = r⁻¹(z − x) ∈ V.
 (⊇) Let y ∈ B ∩ V and put z := x + r y. Then z − x = r y ∈ V, and dist(z, x) = ‖r y‖ = r‖y‖ < rR < δ, so z ∈ M by the hypothesis. Also η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(r y) = y because r ≠ 0. So y ∈ η_{x,r}(M).
5. For every r with 0 < r < δ/R, steps 3, 4 and 3 again give
 ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩V} f dHⁿ = ∫_V f dHⁿ.
6. Since δ/R > 0, the interval (0, δ/R) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). By step 5, r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ is eventually equal along 𝓝[>] 0 to the constant ∫_V f dHⁿ, so it tends to that constant (Filter.tendsto_congr' with tendsto_const_nhds). Since f was arbitrary, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V holds. ∎ No measurability of M is used, and the case n = 0, V = {0} needs no special treatment.
